data.body_html:
Feria San Bernabé 2025 (9–15 June) is Marbella's biggest street party – think casetas, flamenco dresses, and fairground lights. But the real insider move? Pair the fair with a boat party from Marbella Marina or Puerto Banús. You get the best of both: a few hours of sun, sea, and cava, then a short taxi ride to the fairground for the evening. Here's how to plan it.

Why a boat party works during Feria San Bernabé

The fair is intense – crowds, noise, and heat. A boat trip gives you a cool, calm escape in the middle of the day. You can anchor off the coast, swim in the Mediterranean, and enjoy a chilled glass of white wine before hitting the casetas. Plus, you get a different perspective of Marbella from the water, with La Concha mountain as your backdrop.

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, just 15 minutes from the fairground. That means you can spend the morning on the water, return to port for a late lunch, and still make it to the fair by early afternoon.

Dates and logistics for Feria San Bernabé 2025

Feria San Bernabé runs from Monday 9 June to Sunday 15 June 2025. The fairground is located in the centre of Marbella, near the old town. The opening night features a spectacular fireworks display, usually around midnight. If you're planning a boat party, aim for a mid-afternoon slot (13:00–17:00) to avoid the worst of the heat and traffic.

From Puerto Banús, it's a 15-minute taxi ride (approx. €15–20). Alternatively, if you're staying on the Golden Mile, you're even closer – just 10 minutes to the marina and 15 to the fair.

Our boats for your Feria boat party

We have a range of vessels to suit different group sizes and budgets. Here's a quick overview:

All other boats (Azimut 58, Ferretti 94, Canados 86, etc.) are available on request via WhatsApp. For larger groups, the Ferretti 94 (29m) or Canados 86 (26m) offer plenty of space for up to 12 guests.

What's included in your charter

Every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). You won't pay extra for anything – just bring your swimsuit and sunscreen.

For the Mangusta 80, a jet ski is also included free of charge – perfect for a bit of adrenaline between swim stops.

Best anchorages near Marbella for a fair-day escape

From Puerto Banús, you can head east towards Marbella's coastline or west towards Estepona. Our favourite spots:

  • Cala del Faro – a quiet cove near Cabopino, ideal for swimming and snorkelling.
  • Cala Cortés – a rocky bay with crystal-clear water, about 15 minutes from Puerto Banús.
  • Río Verde – just off the Golden Mile, you'll see the luxury villas from the water.
  • Marbella Bay – anchor right in front of the old town for a unique view of the fair fireworks.

Your skipper will recommend the best spot based on wind and sea conditions.

How to book for Feria San Bernabé

Fair week is one of the busiest of the year, so book early. You can check availability and book directly on our website, or message us on WhatsApp for a quick response. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), you can book online instantly. For larger yachts, we'll confirm availability and price within minutes.

If you're planning a full day, consider an 8-hour charter (€2,299 for Tier A) – you can cruise to Estepona or Sotogrande for lunch, then return for the fair in the evening.

Tips for a seamless fair + boat day

  • Book a morning slot (10:00–14:00) to avoid the afternoon heat and fair traffic.
  • Wear comfortable shoes for the fair – you'll be on your feet for hours.
  • Bring a light jacket for the evening – sea breezes can be cool.
  • If you're staying in Marbella city centre, taxi to Puerto Banús early to avoid fair-related road closures.
  • Consider a sunset trip (19:00–21:00) to catch the fair lights from the water.
